name: Glendale
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Glendale location, standing out from most of the chain's reviews with a near-uniformly glowing reception. Reviewers highlight spacious luxury recliners, a full bar and food menu, and PX premium large-format screens for a step up on bigger releases. The Infinity Club membership gets specific, detailed praise — unlimited daily movies plus food/beverage discounts, with reviewers noting occasional deep end-of-year membership deals. Multiple servers are named individually for fast, attentive service.
parking_notes: Discounted validated parking is available at a public lot across the street; nearby street parking has posted time limits.

name: Brookhaven
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Brookhaven location (in the Brookhaven, GA area, sometimes described by reviewers as "Atlanta"), used for private premieres and screenings as well as regular showings. Reviewers describe an intimate, upscale atmosphere with comfortable recliners and food that draws consistent praise despite being on the pricier side. One reviewer's recliner only partially reclined — an isolated equipment issue rather than a chain-wide pattern based on other reviews — and one visit noted thin staffing at the door with no one greeting arrivals.

name: Dobbs Ferry
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Dobbs Ferry location, serving the Westchester, NY area, and the most polarized location in this batch — reviews genuinely split rather than trending one direction. On the strongly positive side: food arriving well-timed and all together (a specific improvement reviewers contrast with other dine-in chains), a distinctive front-row seating option of round lounge beds instead of standard recliners, and a documented service-recovery story where management comped a bill and personally checked in after an order mix-up. On the negative side: one visit described the theater as dirty and odd-smelling despite good food, and a separate review describes a nearly hour-long wait for food with billing errors and an unresolved refund request. Parking is tight — the theater shares a busy shopping-area lot with other retail traffic.
parking_notes: Parking can be tight — the theater sits in a busy shopping area shared with other retail and restaurant traffic.

name: Bedford
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Bedford location, opened in a previously-closed theater space. Reviewers describe a striking lobby and consistently attentive, individually-named servers. Seats and tables are described as somewhat worn since they were inherited from the prior operator, but reviewers note they still recline and function well. Food is consistently well-reviewed (the smash burger gets repeat call-outs), and pricing is described as reasonable. Staff mentioned a possible future breakfast/brunch menu in one review, though that wasn't independently confirmed elsewhere.

name: Arlington
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Arlington, TX location. Experience appears to vary significantly by visit: several reviews describe a clean, comfortable, friendly experience with good food and on-time showings, but one review describes a distinctly bad visit — a dirty, bad-smelling auditorium, sticky and crumb-covered seats, and an $80 tab for food described as tasting cheap, freezer-burnt fries, and a warm, ice-less soda, in a nearly empty theater. Staff are described as kind even in the negative review.

name: Reston
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Reston location. Reviewers generally position it as a solid, comfortable "neighborhood" dine-in option — full bar and food menu, attentive staff, and a well-liked Infinity Club membership for frequent moviegoers — rather than a fine-dining-caliber experience, and most reviews rate it accordingly well within that frame. One reviewer's flatbread order arrived as a poorly-made pizza instead, and described the manager's response to the complaint as defensive rather than accommodating.

name: Tysons at the Boro
description: LOOK Dine-In Cinemas' Tysons/McLean location, a former Icon theater being actively upgraded under LOOK's ownership — reviewers mention a new bar, a group-friendly party area, and a fully revamped menu in progress. Seating is fully reclining with adjustable headrests, sound and picture quality are called out as excellent, and the location is noted as accessible: wheelchair seating, an elevator, accessible bar seating, and gender-neutral restroom options. Parking validation covers the garage. The main recurring complaint is understaffing at the first showings of the day, with food options limited until more staff arrive.
accessibility_notes: Reviewers note wheelchair-accessible seating, an elevator, accessible bar seating, and gender-neutral restroom options.
